hotelsBySegment.title: Hotels by segment
hotelsBySegment.content:
H World operates two reporting segments: HWC (H World China, formerly Legacy-Huazhu) and HWI (H World International, formerly Legacy-Deutsche Hospitality, acquired 2020). The segments are on very different scales -- HWC is ~99% of hotel count -- so the chart uses a secondary axis for HWI.

For H World Group Limited: HWC's growth is almost entirely franchised/manachised net-unit additions; HWI is a smaller, part owned-and-leased German-speaking-Europe estate that management has been quietly trimming (net hotel closures in recent quarters) while it focuses on cost and asset-structure optimisation rather than expansion.

What to watch:

  • HWC hotel count growth (the pipeline conversion rate)
  • Whether HWI net additions turn positive or keep shrinking

roomsBySegment.title: Rooms by segment
roomsBySegment.content:
Room count by segment, same HWC/HWI split as hotel count. Average hotel size differs sharply between the two -- HWI hotels run far more rooms each on average, since the European estate skews to larger owned/leased properties versus HWC's franchise-heavy, smaller economy and midscale hotels.

For H World Group Limited: rooms, not hotel count, is the better proxy for the inventory that actually drives RevPAR-based fee and room revenue.

What to watch:

  • Rooms growing faster or slower than hotel count (average hotel size shift)
  • HWI rooms trend versus HWI hotel count trend

intlHotelPerformance.title: International hotel performance
intlHotelPerformance.content:
RevPAR (revenue per available room) = ADR (average daily rate) x occupancy, for the HWI (international, mainly German-speaking Europe) estate only.

For H World Group Limited: HWI RevPAR is reported in EUR-equivalent terms converted to RMB and is far more exposed to European corporate and leisure travel cycles than the China-driven blended figures elsewhere on this dashboard; it also carries the lower margin of an owned/leased (versus franchised) portfolio.

What to watch:

  • Whether RevPAR gains come from rate (ADR) or demand (occupancy)
  • Seasonality -- European leisure travel peaks differ from China's

sameHotelPerformance.title: Same-hotel (comparable) performance
sameHotelPerformance.content:
Same-hotel RevPAR/ADR/occupancy are reported for HWC (H World China) hotels that have been open at least 18 months, stripping out the effect of new-hotel ramp-up and the pipeline's network growth. This is the figure management and analysts use to judge underlying like-for-like pricing power and demand.

For H World Group Limited: the blended RevPAR/ADR/Occupancy KPIs elsewhere on this dashboard mix in newly-opened hotels (which ramp up occupancy over their first 18 months) and can mask a same-hotel slowdown with network growth, or vice versa.

What to watch:

  • Same-hotel RevPAR YoY versus blended RevPAR YoY -- a widening gap means growth is increasingly coming from new units, not like-for-like strength
  • Same-hotel occupancy decline offset by ADR gains (a sign of post-COVID normalisation versus genuine pricing power)

developmentPipeline.title: Development pipeline
developmentPipeline.content:
Signed but not-yet-opened hotels -- the forward view of network growth, split total versus the HWI (international) slice.

For H World Group Limited: the HWI pipeline is a small, single-digit-percent sliver of the total and has mostly run down over 2023-2025 (37 to 19 hotels) before ticking back up in 2026; almost all forward hotel-count growth is signed through HWC (China) franchise/manachise agreements.

What to watch:

  • Pipeline-to-open conversion rate (compare against hotel-count growth a few quarters later)
  • Whether the 2026 uptick in the HWI pipeline is a real re-expansion or noise

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For H World Group Limited (formerly Huazhu Group / China Lodging Group): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For H World Group Limited (formerly Huazhu Group / China Lodging Group): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For H World Group Limited (formerly Huazhu Group / China Lodging Group): read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For H World Group Limited (formerly Huazhu Group / China Lodging Group): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For H World Group Limited (formerly Huazhu Group / China Lodging Group): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For H World Group Limited (formerly Huazhu Group / China Lodging Group): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For H World Group Limited (formerly Huazhu Group / China Lodging Group): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For H World Group Limited (formerly Huazhu Group / China Lodging Group): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For H World Group Limited (formerly Huazhu Group / China Lodging Group): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For H World Group Limited (formerly Huazhu Group / China Lodging Group): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
